newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco says refinery plan on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco says refinery plan on track.

text.p: Comalco Ltd chief executive Terry Palmer on Monday outlined plans for the aluminium producer's 1.0-1.5 million tonnes alumina refinery to be built in either Queensland or Sarawak, Malaysia.
"That project is meeting the required hurdle rates in pretty adverse times," Palmer told a news conference.
He said the design would allow for an expansion to five million tonnes per annum.
Palmer said it was expected a final decision on the site for the refinery would be made later this calendar year, with a view to seeking board approval to begin construction in 1998.
"With this timetable it is likely that we will see first production from this facility in the year 2001," he said.
"We continue to assess two potential locations - Gladstone in Queensland and a site in Sarawak, Malaysia."
Palmer said he was confident the refinery's cost would be less than an industry benchmark of US$1,000 per tonne of capacity.
But he added that this formula was not necessarily appropriate as an alumina refinery had not been built for 15 years.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by mining house RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd.
